### lem-cardinal-operations-are-well-defined — CERTIFY

For the general case, thm-well-ordering-theorem says, “Assume the Axiom of Choice. Then every set X can be well ordered.” The title, Statement, proof, Facts, and remaining Remarks are mathematically consistent with this distinction, and their dependency citations are accurate.

### thm-cardinal-arithmetic-agrees-with-finite-counting — CERTIFY

"1.1 Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and suppose $\alpha \in n$ with $\alpha \approx n$; then $\alpha \in \mathbb{N}$ by [L2], so $\alpha = n$ by [L1], giving $n \in n$, which [L4] forbids; so $n$ is a cardinal. [L1, L2, L3, L4]" "1.2 Suppose $\alpha \in \omega$ with $\alpha \approx \omega$; then $\alpha \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\mathbb{N} \approx \alpha$, which [L1] forbids; so $\omega$ is a cardinal, and claim (a) holds. [L1, L3, L4]"
ASSESSMENT: Correct. Claim (ii) of lem-omega-least-limit-ordinal says, “every natural number is an ordinal, and ω is an ordinal.” Def-ordinal begins, “A set α is an ordinal when both of the following hold,” supplying the cited definition. Adding L3 to steps 1.1 and 1.2 correctly licenses the prerequisite that the objects being shown initial are ordinals. The proof of the finite dictionary and the proof that infinite cardinals are limit ordinals are valid, and the title matches the result.

### thm-every-infinite-cardinal-is-an-aleph — REFUSE
CURRENT TEXT READ: "They do **not** enumerate the values of the power operation: assuming the Axiom of Choice, so that $2^{\aleph_0}$ is a cardinal at all, it is an aleph by clause (a), but which one is not settled by the axioms in use here, and nothing on this page or its companion asserts a value."
ASSESSMENT: The repaired Remark is correct, but Fact L5 still cites the wrong targets for the assertion that a cardinal is infinite exactly when ω is at most that cardinal. Thm-cardinal-arithmetic-agrees-with-finite-counting states, “Every natural number is a cardinal, and ω is a cardinal,” and separately, “Every infinite cardinal is a limit ordinal.” Def-cardinal defines a cardinal as an initial ordinal. Neither target states the finite versus infinite criterion asserted by L5. That exact criterion is stated in def-cardinal-arithmetic, which this item neither declares nor cites. Steps 3.1 and 4.1 use L5, so this is a surviving load-bearing dependency-citation defect.

### thm-tarski-square — CERTIFY
CURRENT TEXT READ: "[L4] For a well-orderable $X$: $X \approx \lvert X \rvert$, the value is a cardinal, equinumerous sets receive the same one ([[lem-cardinality-of-a-well-orderable-set]]); a cardinal $\kappa$ is finite when $\kappa \in \omega$ and infinite when $\omega \subseteq \kappa$, that is $\omega \le \kappa$ ([[def-cardinal-arithmetic]])."
ASSESSMENT: Correct. Lem-cardinality-of-a-well-orderable-set says, “If X is well-orderable there is a least ordinal equinumerous with X,” that this value is a cardinal, and that equinumerous well-orderable sets receive the same value. Def-cardinal-arithmetic states, “A cardinal κ is finite when κ belongs to ω and infinite when ω is contained in κ, that is ω is at most κ.” The repaired Fact therefore preserves the cited domains and hypotheses exactly. The Hartogs argument validly derives a well-order of every infinite set from the square law, and the title and Statement match the proof.
